title: Secrets of the Imagineers
intro: [whispers] Lean in close, everybody. Tonight we're sharing the secrets of the Imagineers: hidden Mickeys, sneaky tunnels and tricks that fool your eyes. [laughs] Don't tell anyone where you heard it!

art.prompt: A dim Imagineer's workshop at night: a drafting table with a castle blueprint, a scale model mountain under a desk lamp, a magnifying glass over three overlapping circles drawn on paper, and a secret door left slightly open Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

categories.title: Easter Egg Hunt
categories.intro: Imagineers aren't the only ones who hide secrets. [chuckles] Animators do it too. Find these movie Easter eggs!

art.prompt: A film reel unspooling across a desk, with a striped yellow rubber ball, a classroom door, a rusty yellow delivery truck toy and a woven basket of painted eggs hidden among the frames Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: This yellow delivery truck from a restaurant in Toy Story pops up in almost every Pixar movie.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is the Pizza Planet truck! [laughs] It even shows up in Brave, carved in wood.

clues.clue: This classroom number from the CalArts animation school hides in many Pixar and Disney films.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is A113! [whispers] It's the classroom where many famous animators studied. Look for it on license plates and doors.

clues.clue: This yellow ball with a red star and a blue stripe first bounced in a Pixar short, and now hides in lots of Pixar films.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Luxo ball! [chuckles] It first appeared in Luxo Jr. in 1986, with the jumping lamp.

clues.clue: At Elsa's coronation in Frozen, look closely and you'll spot this Tangled princess arriving at the castle gate with Flynn Rider.
clues.reveal: [gasps] The correct answer is Rapunzel! She and Flynn got an invite to Arendelle. [laughs] Royal crossover!

clues.clue: The orange carpet pattern in Sid's house in Toy Story copies the carpet from the Overlook Hotel in this horror film.
clues.reveal: [impressed] The correct answer is The Shining! [whispers] Heeere's Sid. True Disney nerd points!

categories.title: Look Closer, Imagineer
categories.intro: Real photos of famous Disney landmarks, each with a secret. [chuckles] Name what you see!

art.prompt: A large magnifying glass hovering over a sunny theme park map, with tiny drawings of a castle, a sphere, a giant tree and a snowy mountain Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: This castle is 189 feet tall, but its upper floors get smaller and smaller to make it look even taller. Name it.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is Cinderella Castle! That's forced perspective. [laughs] Your eyes have been fooled since 1971.

clues.clue: This giant geodesic sphere at Epcot holds a ride through the history of human communication. Name it.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Spaceship Earth! [chuckles] Not a golf ball. Rain runs into gutters inside the sphere, so it never pours on guests.

clues.clue: Imagineers covered this Animal Kingdom icon with more than 300 animal carvings. Name it.
clues.reveal: [gasps] The correct answer is the Tree of Life! There are 337 animals carved into it. [whispers] Bring binoculars.

clues.clue: A brownish stripe painted down the middle of this Magic Kingdom land's street stands in for the sewage that ran through colonial streets.
clues.reveal: [laughs] The correct answer is Liberty Square! It's history, but a little gross. [chuckles] That's also why the land is famously short on restrooms.

clues.clue: Inside this Disneyland mountain, near the top, there's a small basketball hoop for cast members to play on.
clues.reveal: [impressed] The correct answer is the Matterhorn! The climbers in the show used to shoot hoops on their breaks. True Disney nerd points!

categories.title: Imagineer Speak
categories.intro: Imagineers have their own words. [laughs] Let's see if you speak the language!

art.prompt: A chalkboard covered in arrows, sketches of a tall tower at the end of a long street and little hot dogs drawn in the margins, with a coffee mug and colored pencils on a ledge Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: At Disney parks, the people who work there aren't called employees. They're called this.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is cast members! Because the park is a show, and everyone has a role. [laughs] Even the popcorn sweepers!

clues.clue: Imagineers use this trick to make buildings look taller by shrinking the upper floors.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is forced perspective! [chuckles] Main Street's top floors are smaller too. Your eyes do the rest.

clues.clue: Walt called a tall landmark that pulls guests down a street, like a castle, by this funny name that also means a hot dog.
clues.reveal: [laughs] The correct answer is a weenie! Like waving a hot dog in front of a dog. Walk toward the castle, folks!

clues.clue: Imagineering began as WED Enterprises. The W, E and D stood for this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Walter Elias Disney! [chuckles] Walt literally put his initials on the company.

clues.clue: Imagineers call the first stage of a project, when any idea is allowed, by this two-word name.
clues.reveal: [impressed] The correct answer is blue sky! No budget, no limits, just dreams. True Imagineering points!

categories.title: Secrets in Plain Sight
categories.intro: Hidden Mickeys and secret tributes, right in front of your eyes. [whispers] Are you looking closely?

art.prompt: A sunlit old-fashioned street at dawn with painted second-story windows, a single glowing lamp in one window and three round pebbles arranged on the sidewalk Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: A classic Hidden Mickey is made of three of these shapes: one big one and two small ones.
clues.reveal: [excited] The correct answer is circles! One for the head and two for the ears. [laughs] Now you'll see them everywhere.

clues.clue: In the Haunted Mansion's ballroom, a Hidden Mickey is made of these on the dining table.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is plates! [chuckles] One plate and two saucers. Ghosts know their Mickeys.

clues.clue: The upper windows on Main Street, U.S.A. are painted with fake business names that honor these people.
clues.answer: People who helped build the parks
accept: people who helped build the parks
choices: People who helped build the parks
clues.reveal: The correct answer is people who helped build the parks! [whispers] It's like the closing credits of a movie, painted on glass.

clues.clue: At Disneyland, this is kept lit in Walt's apartment window above the fire station, in his honor.
clues.reveal: [sighs] The correct answer is a lamp! It means Walt is still with us in the park. [chuckles] Pretty magical.

clues.clue: A Main Street window at Magic Kingdom honors Walt's dad, Elias Disney, with this job title.
clues.reveal: [impressed] The correct answer is contractor! Elias Disney really built houses. True Disney nerd points!

categories.title: Under the Castle
categories.intro: There's a secret world underneath Magic Kingdom. [whispers] Shh. Let's go downstairs.

art.prompt: A long underground service tunnel with color-striped walls, pipes running along the ceiling, a rolling clothes rack of colorful costumes and a sign-free directional arrow painted on the floor Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: Walt didn't want guests to see a cowboy walking through this futuristic land, so cast members use secret tunnels.
clues.reveal: [laughs] The correct answer is Tomorrowland! A cowboy in the future? Walt said no way.

clues.clue: Magic Kingdom's secret tunnels are called utilidors. That word is short for this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is utility corridors! [chuckles] Not as fancy as it sounds. Lots of pipes.

clues.clue: The utilidor walls are painted in different colors so cast members know where they are. The colors match this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the lands above them! [excited] No map needed. Just follow the colors.

clues.clue: The utilidors aren't really underground. They're on the ground floor, which means the Magic Kingdom park is on this level.
clues.reveal: [gasps] The correct answer is the second floor! You've been upstairs this whole time. [laughs] Mind blown.

clues.clue: Magic Kingdom's trash zooms through underground tubes at up to 60 miles per hour, using a system called this four-letter acronym.
clues.reveal: [impressed] The correct answer is AVAC! Automated vacuum collection. [laughs] Trash just goes woosh. True Disney nerd points!
